extracted.intended_audience: SymPy contributors and Python developers writing SymPy docstrings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for writing, formatting, and importing docstrings for SymPy modules, classes (including mathematical function classes), methods, and functions so they render correctly in Sphinx and are useful to end users and developers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Docstring requirement for public API
rubrics_metrics.description: Every public function, class, method, and module should have a docstring that describes what it does.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Module-level docstrings should discuss the purpose and scope of the module and give a high-level example. A public function is one intended for end-users. If unsure whether something is public, prefer documenting it. Instructions for importing public docstrings into Sphinx are given later in the guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Docstrings for private functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Private functions (intended only for use inside SymPy) are less important to document but still benefit other developers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Private functions usually begin with an underscore; presence in __init__.py indicates public, but this is not absolute—use context. Keep private-docstring content concise and put anything important in class-level or public docstrings since private docstrings are not pulled into Sphinx.

rubrics_metrics.name: Docstrings are for users (not code comments)
rubrics_metrics.description: Docstrings should contain information aimed at users of the function. Comments specific to the code or other notes that would only distract users should go in comments in the code, not in docstrings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on user-facing behavior and API; implementation specifics belong in inline code comments or developer docs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples required and primary
rubrics_metrics.description: Every docstring should have examples that show how the function works. Examples are the most important part of a docstring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A single clear example showing input and output can be more helpful than a long paragraph. Treat doctests as examples that happen to be tested; they should demonstrate the API and be human-readable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human-oriented prose
rubrics_metrics.description: Docstrings should describe what the function does in plain English; prioritize human readers over doctest machinery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write examples and descriptions with human readability in mind. Although doctests are executed, examples should be designed to teach users, not merely satisfy tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sphinx primary but not sole consumer
rubrics_metrics.description: Sphinx is the primary way users consume docstrings, but help() and IPython (?) are also used and people may read source code directly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write docstrings so they render well in Sphinx and remain useful via help() or direct source-reading. Private method docstrings are shown by help(), so consider that audience too.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use triple double quotes
rubrics_metrics.description: Always use """ triple double quotes around docstrings. Use r""" raw triple double quotes if you use any backslashes in your docstrings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistent use avoids parsing issues. Use raw strings when including LaTeX/math or backslashes to avoid escape processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blank line before closing quotes
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a blank line before the docstring’s closing quotes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures Sphinx and other tools render spacing correctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Line length limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Lines should not be longer than 80 characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wrap long lines, and ensure wrapped code remains valid Python in doctests (see doctest continuation rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Class-level docstring placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Always write class-level docstrings under the class definition line, as that is better to read in the source code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not put the class docstring elsewhere. Mention important methods in the class docstring but put detailed docs in each method's docstring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use doctests for code examples
rubrics_metrics.description: :: creates code blocks, which are rarely used in the docstrings. Any code example with example Python should be put in a doctest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Doctests are preferred because they are rendered and can be executed. Only use :: blocks for non-Python block formatting rarely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use numpydoc extension for section underlining
rubrics_metrics.description: In order to make section underlining work nicely in docstrings, numpydoc Sphinx extension is used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow numpydoc conventions (headings underlined with = signs) to ensure consistent formatting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Always verify Sphinx rendering
rubrics_metrics.description: Always check that the final version as rendered by Sphinx looks correct in the HTML.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steps: Make sure the docstring is imported into Sphinx, build the Sphinx docs (cd doc; make html), ensure Sphinx reports no errors, and open the built HTML in _build/html to inspect formatting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supported section headings and order
rubrics_metrics.description: Preferred sections in this order: Single-Sentence Summary, Explanation, Examples, Parameters, See Also, References.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Single-Sentence Summary and Examples sections are required for every docstring. Do not change the names of these supported sections. Use only necessary sections to avoid clutter; aim for minimal information needed to understand the function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-Sentence Summary rules
rubrics_metrics.description: This section is required for every docstring. It consists of a one-line sentence ending in a period that describes the function, class, or method’s effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No heading is necessary for this section. Deprecation warnings should go directly after the Single-Sentence Summary using the .. deprecated:: Sphinx directive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deprecation placement and format
rubrics_metrics.description: Deprecation warnings should go directly after the Single-Sentence Summary and be written as a deprecated Sphinx directive (.. deprecated::).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the version and recommended alternative and a short explanation. Example in guide shows formatting and placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanation section usage
rubrics_metrics.description: The Explanation section is encouraged and should be labeled 'Explanation' underlined with equals signs when included. It consists of a more elaborate description when the single-sentence summary is insufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Explanation to clarify functionality in several sentences or paragraphs; omit if unnecessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples section rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The Examples section is required and must be labeled 'Examples'. It consists of examples that show how the function works, called doctests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Doctests should be complicated enough to demonstrate the API but simple enough for users to understand. Always include a blank line before the doctest; separate multiple examples with blank lines; comments explaining examples should have blank lines above and below them. Treat doctests as examples, not unit tests. Run ./bin/doctest and ./bin/coverage_doctest.py to check examples and doctest coverage. Skip testing only if impossible by adding a special comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Doctest line-wrapping conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: If an example is longer than 80 characters, it should be line wrapped so that they are still valid Python code, using ... continuation as in a Python prompt. The output of a command can also be line wrapped; no ... should be used in this case. The doctester automatically accepts output that is line wrapped.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When breaking input lines, put ... on continuation lines like the Python prompt. For output wrapping, do not add ...; the doctest runner accepts wrapped output automatically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imports and symbol definition in examples
rubrics_metrics.description: In a doctest, write imports like 'from sympy import ...' instead of 'import sympy' or 'from sympy import *'. To define symbols, use 'from sympy.abc import x' unless the name is not in sympy.abc (e.g., when assumptions are needed), in which case use symbols('x y').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This encourages explicit, consistent examples and avoids namespace issues. Use sympy.abc for simple symbol creation when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parameters section rules
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have parameters listed in parentheses after a function, class, or method name, you must include a Parameters section labeled 'Parameters'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe arguments, keywords, and types. Enclose variables in double backticks. The colon must be preceded by a space or omitted if the type is absent. Be precise about types. Use 'optional' for optional keyword params (show defaults). For parameters with fixed sets, list values in braces with default first. Combine parameters with identical type/description. Incorrect formatting will render documentation incorrectly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Returns section as own heading
rubrics_metrics.description: If you wish to include a Returns section, write it as its own section with its own heading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not conflate return descriptions into the Parameters or other sections; use a dedicated 'Returns' heading when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: See Also section rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The See Also section is encouraged and should be labeled 'See Also'. It consists of a listing of related functions, classes, and methods (SymPy objects only).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Related items may be concise fragments. If a description spans more than one line, indent subsequent lines. Do not reference classes using class:Classname, class:`Classname`, or :class:`Classname`—refer only by name. Links to other objects should be embedded as hyperlinks in the text; external resources belong in References.

rubrics_metrics.name: References section rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The References section is encouraged, labeled 'References', and should list references cited anywhere in the docstring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include online resources, papers, and printed resources that augment the docstring but are not required to understand it. Number references starting from 1 in citation order. For online resources, link only to stable, free sites such as Wikipedia, Wolfram MathWorld, or NIST DLMF. For papers, include citation, authors, title, journal, year, pages, and include DOI when available (clickable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Math function class docstring math and conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Docstrings for classes that are mathematical functions should include a mathematical definition of the function using LaTeX math and other math-specific guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use $$ for inline math and .. math:: for display math (display math for main definition). Variable names in formulas should match parameter names and LaTeX formatting should match SymPy pretty printing. Mention domain of definition (especially if not complex numbers). If multiple conventions exist in literature, clearly specify which is used. Include important mathematical facts (or demonstrate them in Examples) but avoid overly long mathematical discussions; references may be used for details. Place the docstring at class level; the 'eval' method should not have a docstring; private methods need not be documented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best practices and tone
rubrics_metrics.description: When writing docstrings, follow the same formatting, style, and tone preferences as narrative documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the project's 'Best Practices for Writing Documentation' and 'Formatting, Style, and Tone' guidelines for consistent voice and style across SymPy docs and docstrings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importing docstrings into Sphinx
rubrics_metrics.description: Docstrings must be imported into the Sphinx docs using RST directives in module RST files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use .. module:: to set the namespace to a particular submodule and then .. autoclass:: or .. autofunction:: (relative to that submodule) to import docstrings. Avoid using full paths that break viewcode extension. All files in doc/src/modules/ should follow this format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-referencing SymPy objects
rubrics_metrics.description: Text referencing another SymPy function should be formatted so Sphinx creates an automatic cross-reference link using RST cross-reference syntax.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For objects included in 'from sympy import *' use :obj:`~.name()` (tilde shortens displayed name, dot helps Sphinx find it). The trailing parentheses indicate callable convention. Use :obj: generally since it works for any object type. If multiple names exist use the full qualified name. For objects not included in 'from sympy import *' (e.g., submodule objects) use the fully qualified name (no ~). Use :obj:`custom text<object>` to create link text. If an object cannot be linked (built-ins, external modules, or names specific to text), mark it with double backticks instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct type-specific cross-ref usage
rubrics_metrics.description: If you use one of the type-specific identifiers like :func:, ensure the type is correct (:func: only refers to Python functions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer :obj: if unsure. For classes use :class:, for methods use :method:, etc. Incorrect type usage can cause Sphinx errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-reference troubleshooting guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: If Sphinx gives cross-reference warnings or errors, follow troubleshooting steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make sure syntax is correct, spellings are correct, the referenced function/object is actually included in Sphinx docs (add it to the appropriate RST if not), and use fully qualified names when necessary. If you cannot resolve cross-reference problems, submit your pull request and ask reviewers for help.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling ambiguous cross-reference targets
rubrics_metrics.description: If Sphinx warns 'more than one target found' for a cross-reference (e.g., subs()), use a fully qualified name to disambiguate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may still use ~ to shorten the final display, e.g., :obj:`~sympy.core.basic.Basic.subs` will display as Basic.subs while referencing the fully qualified target.

rubrics_metrics.name: Line number warning caveat
rubrics_metrics.description: Sphinx line numbers for warnings in Python files are relative to the top of the docstring, not the file itself, and are often not completely correct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a warning shows a line number, search within the docstring to find the relevant part; expect to scan around the indicated area because of a Sphinx bug.
